linkages: Workers linked to their partners (marriages and registered partnerships), whose education, earnings and worker type are observed.
Workers linked to their mother and father, whose education, net wealth, delinquency and worker type are observed.
The European Labor Force Survey is linked to the Danish administrative records.
Workers linked to firms in matched employer-employee data (AKM worker fixed effects, firm-level value added, separation rates).

sample.unit_of_observation: Worker (person); person-year for the clustering moments and for the consumption regression of equation (2)
selection_rules: Exclude workers with weak labor force attachment.
Restrict to ages 30-65 to avoid the misclassification of students, for example due to summer jobs.
Data start in 2008 (data availability) and end in 2018, two years before the pandemic, to test for mean reversion.

construction_notes: Worker types are assigned by k-means clustering on 13 moments summarising each worker's labour market experience: the shares of matches in five duration bins (1-3M, 3-6M, 6-12M, 12-24M, 24+M), the shares of non-employment spells in five duration bins (0-1M, 1-3M, 3-6M, 6-12M, 12+M), jobs per month, the non-employment rate and the unemployment rate.
Job-to-job transitions are considered a non-employment duration of zero months.
Employment status and job spell durations come from wage payment records (BFL); unemployment status from social security benefit records (DREAM).

Net wealth includes housing and debt; delinquencies and interest payments are computed for observed non-housing debt, and 'No loans found' is the share of households for whom such debt is not observed.
'Ever delinquent' includes delayed debt payments; 'Partner' includes both marriages and registered partnerships; 'Had partner' includes both divorces and death.
Health visit variables refer to the share of the population that ever had a visit; data sources are SYIN and SSSY.
Mincer residuals and AKM worker fixed-effects are estimated on the entire population without sample restrictions.
Consumption is imputed from each household's annual balance sheets, which contain all labor and capital income and are used for tax purposes.

The consumption gap by employment status is not observed directly: it is imputed by regressing log annual consumption on the annual unemployment rate with worker and year fixed effects (equation (2)), separately by worker type.
All rates in the model calibration are at quarterly frequency.
In the model the coefficient of relative risk aversion sigma is set to 2 and the matching function is q(theta) = theta^(-alpha) with alpha = 0.5.
